steps.announcement: The initial six-element unsorted array is [2, 4, 1, 0, 3, 5].
steps.explanation: The array is [2, 4, 1, 0, 3, 5]. All elements lie in the pending index range [0, 5]. No pivot has been chosen and no position is fixed.
steps.key_state: The initial array is [2, 4, 1, 0, 3, 5]. The pending index range is [0, 5], with no pivot chosen yet.
steps.title: Initial unsorted array

steps.announcement: Choose the first element, 2, as the pivot for the first partition.
steps.explanation: In the index range [0, 5], choose the leftmost element, 2 at index 0, as the pivot. The array is still [2, 4, 1, 0, 3, 5]. No rearrangement has occurred and the final pivot position is undetermined.
steps.key_state: The array is [2, 4, 1, 0, 3, 5]. The pivot 2 at index 0 has been chosen, but partitioning has yet to occur.
steps.title: Choose 2 as the first pivot

steps.announcement: The first partition is complete. Pivot 2 is fixed at index 2, leaving a left and a right subrange.
steps.explanation: After the first partition, the array is [1, 0, 2, 4, 3, 5]. Only the pivot 2 at index 2 is fixed. The pending index ranges are [0, 1] and [3, 5], containing [1, 0] and [4, 3, 5], respectively.
steps.key_state: The array is [1, 0, 2, 4, 3, 5]. Only index 2 is fixed. The pending index ranges are [0, 1] and [3, 5].
steps.title: Finish the first partition and fix pivot 2

steps.announcement: Show the left subrange [0, 1] and right subrange [3, 5] side by side at the next recursion level.
steps.explanation: Expand two subproblems at the next level. The index range [0, 1] contains [1, 0], and [3, 5] contains [4, 3, 5]. The array is still [1, 0, 2, 4, 3, 5], with only index 2 fixed. This state expands the subproblems but has yet to partition either.
steps.key_state: The array is [1, 0, 2, 4, 3, 5]. Only index 2 is fixed. Both subproblems at the next level have been expanded but have yet to finish partitioning.
steps.title: Expand the left and right subproblems

steps.announcement: The subproblem pivots 1 and 4 are fixed at indices 1 and 4, respectively. Only three single-element ranges remain.
steps.explanation: The left subarray [1, 0] uses pivot 1 and becomes [0, 1]. The right subarray [4, 3, 5] uses pivot 4 and becomes [3, 4, 5]. The full array is now [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5], with pivots fixed at indices 1, 2, and 4. The ranges [0, 0], [3, 3], and [5, 5] each contain one element and have yet to be marked complete.
steps.key_state: The array is [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. Pivots are fixed at indices 1, 2, and 4. The single-element ranges at indices 0, 3, and 5 still await completion marks.
steps.title: Finish partitioning each subproblem

steps.announcement: Recursion stops on the single-element subranges. All six positions are fixed, completing the sort.
steps.explanation: The ranges [0, 0], [3, 3], and [5, 5] all satisfy the base case of length at most 1. All positions from 0 through 5 are fixed. The final array is [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. No merge is needed, and sorting is complete.
steps.key_state: Sorting is complete. The array is [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5], with all positions from 0 through 5 fixed.
steps.title: Finish the single-element ranges to complete the sort

prose.summary: Six states show the partition results by recursion level. Side-by-side subproblems do not run in parallel. The code calls the left before the right.
prose.title: Quicksort recursion overview

context: The input array is [2, 4, 1, 0, 3, 5], with indices 0 through 5. Each partition takes the leftmost element of the current subarray as the pivot. After rearrangement, all values on the left are at most the pivot and all on the right are at least the pivot, placing it in its final sorted position.
description: Blue cells mark pivots in their final positions. Downward arrows lead to the resulting subranges. Side-by-side subproblems show recursion levels and dependencies rather than parallel execution. The code recurses on the left first, then the right. The overview shows each partition's input and output without detailing pointer movements or individual swaps.
The table below lists the three partitions of ranges longer than 1. The ranges and final pivot indices refer to the full array. The input subarray and partition result columns list element values.

From the recursive bounds in the code, fixing pivot 1 at index 1 leaves the empty range [2, 1] to its right, which terminates immediately. The figure shows only the other three subranges, each with one element.

frames.explanation: After three partitions, pivot values 1, 2, and 4 are fixed at indices 1, 2, and 4, respectively. The single-element ranges at indices 0, 3, and 5 return immediately. The full array is [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. Recursion stops at length 1 or less, and no merge is needed.
frames.title: Quicksort recursion overview

summary: Each partition fixes the pivot in its final position. Recursively partition the left and right subarrays until each remaining range has length at most 1.
title: Quicksort recursion overview
